<h1 id="render-public-api-audit-logs">Audit Logs</h1>

[Audit Logs](https://render.com/docs/audit-logs) allow you to retrieve audit logs for workspaces and organizations.
These logs provide a trail of actions and changes made to your resources.


## List workspace audit logs

<a id="opIdlist-owner-audit-logs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/owners/string/audit-logs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /owners/{ownerId}/audit-logs`

Retrieve audit logs for a specific workspace with optional filtering and pagination.


<h3 id="list-workspace-audit-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startTime|query|string(date-time)|false|Start time for filtering audit logs (ISO 8601 format)|
|endTime|query|string(date-time)|false|End time for filtering audit logs (ISO 8601 format)|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to query logs for. Backward will return most recent logs first.<br>Forward will start with the oldest logs in the time range.<br>|
|cursor|query|string|false|The position in the result list to start from when fetching paginated results. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of audit log items to return. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|ownerId|path|string|true|The ID of the workspace to return resources for|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|forward|
|direction|backward|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "cursor": "string",
    "auditLog": {
      "id": "aud-123456789",
      "timestamp": "2023-10-01T12:00:00Z",
      "event": "CreateServerEvent",
      "status": "success",
      "actor": {
        "type": "user",
        "email": "user@example.com",
        "id": "usr-123456789"
      },
      "metadata": {
        "service": "srv-123456789",
        "field": "env_vars"
      }
    }
  }
]
```

<h1 id="render-public-api-blueprints">Blueprints</h1>

[Blueprints](https://render.com/docs/infrastructure-as-code) allow you to define your resources in a `render.yaml` file and automatically sync changes to your Render services.
The API gives control over how your Blueprints are used to create and manage resources.


## List Blueprints

<a id="opIdlist-blueprints"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/blueprints \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /blueprints`

List Blueprints for the specified workspaces. If no workspaces are provided, returns all Blueprints the API key has access to.


<h3 id="list-blueprints-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ownerId|query|[string]|false|The ID of the workspaces to return resources for|
|cursor|query|string|false|The position in the result list to start from when fetching paginated results. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items to return. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "blueprint": {
      "id": "exs-cph1rs3idesc73a2b2mg",
      "name": "string",

      "repo": "string",

]
```

## Validate Blueprint

<a id="opIdvalidate-blueprint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/blueprints/validate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'ownerId=tea-cjnxpkdhshc73d12t9i0' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /blueprints/validate`

Validate a `render.yaml` Blueprint file without creating or modifying any resources. This endpoint checks the syntax and structure of the Blueprint, validates that all required fields are present, and returns a plan indicating the resources that would be created.

Requests to this endpoint use `Content-Type: multipart/form-data`. The request body (including the Blueprint file) cannot exceed 10MB in size.


> Body parameter

```yaml
ownerId: tea-cjnxpkdhshc73d12t9i0
file: string
```

<h3 id="validate-blueprint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» ownerId|body|string|true|The ID of the workspace to validate against. Obtain your workspace ID from its Settings page in the Render Dashboard.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The render.yaml file to validate, as a binary file.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "valid": true,
  "errors": [
    {
      "path": "string",
      "error": "string",
      "line": 0,
      "column": 0
    }
  ],
  "plan": {
    "services": [
      "string"
    ],
    "databases": [
      "string"
    ],
    "keyValue": [
      "string"
    ],
    "envGroups": [
      "string"
    ],
    "workflows": [
      "string"
    ],
    "totalActions": 0
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "code": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "code": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "code": "string"
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "code": "string"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "message": "rate limit exceeded"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="validate-blueprint-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Validation complete|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|The request could not be understood by the server.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authorization information is missing or invalid.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have permissions for the requested resource. If a scoped API token does not satisfy the endpoint's minimum scope requirements, the response has code insufficient_token_scope and its message lists all minimum required scopes. Broader scopes that include their permissions also satisfy the requirements. Passing this check does not guarantee access to the requested resource or to conditional operations.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|413|Payload Too Large|The request body exceeded the maximum allowed size.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate limit has been surpassed.<br><br>Rate-limited endpoints also return `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, and<br>`RateLimit-Reset` on successful responses so clients can track their remaining quota.<br>|[error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|An unexpected server error has occurred.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="validate-blueprint-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|valid|boolean|true|none|If `true`, the Blueprint validated successfully. If `false`, at least one validation error occurred.|
|errors|[object]|false|none|A list of validation errors. Only present if `valid` is `false`.|
|» path|string|false|none|The path to the field with the error (e.g., `services[0].plan`)|
|» error|string|true|none|The error message|
|» line|integer|false|none|The line number in the YAML file (1-indexed)|
|» column|integer|false|none|The column number in the YAML file (1-indexed)|
|plan|object|false|none|A summary of the resources that would be created as part of the Blueprint. Only present if `valid` is `true`.|
|» services|[string]|false|none|The names of services that would be created as part of the Blueprint.|
|» databases|[string]|false|none|The names of Render Postgres databases that would be created as part of the Blueprint.|
|» keyValue|[string]|false|none|The names of Render Key Value instances that would be created as part of the Blueprint.|
|» envGroups|[string]|false|none|The names of environment groups that would be created as part of the Blueprint.|
|» workflows|[string]|false|none|The names of workflows that would be created as part of the Blueprint.|
|» totalActions|integer|false|none|The total number of actions that would be performed by the Blueprint. In addition to created resources, this includes modifications to individual configuration fields.|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|429|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before retrying the request.|
|429|RateLimit-Limit|integer||Maximum number of requests allowed in the current window.|
|429|RateLimit-Remaining|integer||Number of requests remaining in the current window. Always `0` for this response.|
|429|RateLimit-Reset|integer||Seconds until the current rate limit window resets.|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BearerAuth
</aside>

`GET /services/{serviceId}/custom-domains`

List a particular service's custom domains that match the provided filters. If no filters are provided, all custom domains for the service are returned.

## Create dedicated IP set

<a id="opIdcreate-dedicated-ip"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/dedicated-ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "ownerId": "string",
    "region": "oregon",
    "environmentIds": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /dedicated-ips`

Create a dedicated IP set. Provisioning an IP set is asynchronous. The response returns immediately with `status: CREATING` and `ips: []`. When provisioning completes, status changes to `RUNNING` and `ips` contains your assigned addresses.

If `environmentIds` is omitted or empty, this IP set applies to all services in the workspace in the selected region. Otherwise, it applies only to services in the listed environments in that region.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "ownerId": "string",
  "region": "oregon",
  "environmentIds": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-dedicated-ip-set-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[dedicatedIPPOST](#schemadedicatedippost)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name for the dedicated IP set.|
|» description|body|string|false|Free-form description for the dedicated IP set.|
|» ownerId|body|string|true|The ID of the workspace that will own this dedicated IP set.|
|» region|body|[region](#schemaregion)|true|Defaults to "oregon"|
|» environmentIds|body|[string]|false|Environments to scope the dedicated IP set to. If omitted or empty, it applies to all services in the workspace within its region.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» region|frankfurt|
|» region|oregon|
|» region|ohio|
|» region|singapore|
|» region|virginia|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "ownerId": "string",
  "region": "oregon",
  "environmentIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ips": [
    "string"
  ],
  "status": "UNKNOWN",
  "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

```json
  "id": "string",

  "code": "string"
}
```

<h1 id="render-public-api-deploys">Deploys</h1>

[Deploys](https://render.com/docs/deploys) are the process of updating your service with new code or configuration.
These endpoints allow you to retrieve data on the deploys of your services
as well as trigger new deploys and rollbacks. Most changes to your service
will require a new deploy to take effect.

To create and manage services, use the `Services` endpoints.


## List deploys

<a id="opIdlist-deploys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/services/string/deploys \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /services/{serviceId}/deploys`

List deploys matching the provided filters. If no filters are provided, all deploys for the service are returned.


<h3 id="list-deploys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|query|[[deployStatus](#schemadeploystatus)]|false|Filter for deploys with the specified statuses|
|createdBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for deploys created before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|createdAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for deploys created after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|updatedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for deploys updated before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|updatedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for deploys updated after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|finishedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for deploys finished before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|finishedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for deploys finished after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|cursor|query|string|false|The position in the result list to start from when fetching paginated results. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items to return. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|serviceId|path|string|true|The ID of the service|

## Trigger deploy

<a id="opIdcreate-deploy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/services/string/deploys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "buildId": "string",
    "clearCache": "do_not_clear",
    "commitId": "string",
    "imageUrl": "string",
    "deployMode": "build_and_deploy"
  }'
```

`POST /services/{serviceId}/deploys`

Trigger a deploy for the service with the provided ID.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "buildId": "string",
  "clearCache": "do_not_clear",
  "commitId": "string",
  "imageUrl": "string",
  "deployMode": "build_and_deploy"
}
```

<h3 id="trigger-deploy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serviceId|path|string|true|The ID of the service|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» buildId|body|string|false|The ID of the build to deploy. Cannot be combined with `commitId`, `imageUrl`, or `deployMode`.<br>|
|» clearCache|body|string|false|If `clear`, Render clears the service's build cache before deploying. This can be useful if you're experiencing issues with your build.|
|» commitId|body|string|false|The SHA of a specific Git commit to deploy for a service. Defaults to the latest commit on the service's connected branch. Cannot be combined with `buildId`, `imageUrl`, or `deployMode: deploy_only`.<br><br>Note that deploying a specific commit with this endpoint does not disable autodeploys for the service.<br><br>You can toggle autodeploys for your service with the [Update service](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-service) endpoint or in the Render Dashboard.<br><br>Not supported for cron jobs.<br>|
|» imageUrl|body|string|false|The URL of the image to deploy for an image-backed service. Cannot be combined with `buildId`, `commitId`, or `deployMode: deploy_only`.<br><br>The host, repository, and image name all must match the currently configured image for the service.<br>|
|» deployMode|body|[DeployMode](#schemadeploymode)|false|Deployment mode controlling build and deploy behavior.<br><br>Defaults to `build_and_deploy` when not specified.<br><br>**Validation:** `deployMode` cannot be combined with `buildId`. `deploy_only` cannot be combined with `commitId`, `imageUrl`, or `clearCache`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» clearCache|clear|
|» clearCache|do_not_clear|
|» deployMode|deploy_only|
|» deployMode|build_and_deploy|

## Roll back deploy

<a id="opIdrollback-deploy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/services/string/rollback \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "deployId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /services/{serviceId}/rollback`

Trigger a rollback to a previous deploy of the specified service.

Triggering a rollback with this endpoint does not disable autodeploys for the service. This means an autodeploy might restore changes you had intentionally rolled back.

You can toggle autodeploys for your service with the [Update service](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-service) endpoint or in the Render Dashboard.

## Restore snapshot

<a id="opIdrestore-snapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/disks/string/snapshots/restore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "snapshotKey": "string",
    "instanceId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /disks/{diskId}/snapshots/restore`

Restore a persistent disk to an available snapshot.

**This operation is irreversible.** It will overwrite the current disk data. It might also trigger a service deploy.

Snapshot keys returned from the [List snapshots](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/list-snapshots) endpoint expire after 24 hours. If a snapshot key has expired, query the endpoint again for a new key.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "snapshotKey": "string",
  "instanceId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="restore-snapshot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|diskId|path|string|true|The ID of the disk|
|body|body|[snapshotRestorePOST](#schemasnapshotrestorepost)|true|none|
|» snapshotKey|body|string|true|none|
|» instanceId|body|[instanceId](#schemainstanceid)|false|When a service with a disk is scaled, the instanceId is used to identify the instance that the disk is attached to. Each instance's disks get their own snapshots, and can be restored separately.|

<h1 id="render-public-api-key-value">Key Value</h1>

[Key Value](https://render.com/docs/key-value) allows you to interact with your Render Key Value instances.


## List Key Value instances

<a id="opIdlist-key-value"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/key-value \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /key-value`

List Key Value instances matching the provided filters. If no filters are provided, all Key Value instances are returned.


<h3 id="list-key-value-instances-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Filter by name|
|region|query|[[region](#schemaregion)]|false|Filter by resource region|
|createdBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources created before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|createdAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources created after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|updatedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources updated before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|updatedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources updated after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|ownerId|query|[string]|false|The ID of the workspaces to return resources for|
|environmentId|query|[string]|false|Filter for resources that belong to an environment|
|cursor|query|string|false|The position in the result list to start from when fetching paginated results. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items to return. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|

## Create Key Value instance

<a id="opIdcreate-key-value"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/key-value \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "ownerId": "string",
    "plan": "free",
    "region": "oregon",
    "environmentId": "string",
    "maxmemoryPolicy": "noeviction",
    "persistenceMode": "journal_snapshot",
    "ipAllowList": [
      {
        "cidrBlock": "string",
        "description": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /key-value`

Create a new Key Value instance.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "ownerId": "string",
  "plan": "free",
  "region": "oregon",
  "environmentId": "string",
  "maxmemoryPolicy": "noeviction",
  "persistenceMode": "journal_snapshot",
  "ipAllowList": [
    {
      "cidrBlock": "string",
      "description": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-key-value-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[keyValuePOSTInput](#schemakeyvaluepostinput)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the Key Value instance|
|» ownerId|body|string|true|The ID of the owner of the Key Value instance|
|» plan|body|[keyValuePlan](#schemakeyvalueplan)|true|none|
|» region|body|[region](#schemaregion)|false|Defaults to "oregon"|
|» environmentId|body|string|false|none|
|» maxmemoryPolicy|body|[maxmemoryPolicy](#schemamaxmemorypolicy)|false|The eviction policy for the Key Value instance|
|» persistenceMode|body|[persistenceMode](#schemapersistencemode)|false|The persistence mode for the Key Value instance. The default for paid instances is journal_snapshot (both journaling and snapshots). Only turn off persistence if you're using this Key Value instance as a cache and are okay with losing data. Free instances do not have persistence.|
|» ipAllowList|body|[[cidrBlockAndDescription](#schemacidrblockanddescription)]|false|none|

```bash
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "plan": "free",
    "maxmemoryPolicy": "noeviction",
    "persistenceMode": "journal_snapshot",
    "ipAllowList": [
      {
        "cidrBlock": "string",
        "description": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /key-value/{redisId}`

Update a Key Value instance by ID. Note that changing your plan, max memory policy, or persistence mode will restart your Key Value instance.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "plan": "free",
  "maxmemoryPolicy": "noeviction",
  "persistenceMode": "journal_snapshot",
  "ipAllowList": [
    {
      "cidrBlock": "string",
      "description": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-key-value-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|redisId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[keyValuePATCHInput](#schemakeyvaluepatchinput)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the Key Value instance|
|» plan|body|[keyValuePlan](#schemakeyvalueplan)|false|none|
|» maxmemoryPolicy|body|[maxmemoryPolicy](#schemamaxmemorypolicy)|false|The eviction policy for the Key Value instance|
|» persistenceMode|body|[persistenceMode](#schemapersistencemode)|false|The persistence mode for the Key Value instance. The default for paid instances is journal_snapshot (both journaling and snapshots). Only turn off persistence if you're using this Key Value instance as a cache and are okay with losing data. <h1 id="render-public-api-logs">Logs</h1>

[Logs](https://render.com/docs/logging) allow you to retrieve logs for your services, Postgres databases, and redis instances.
You can query for logs or subscribe to logs in real-time via a websocket.


## List logs

<a id="opIdlist-logs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.render.com/v1/logs?ownerId=string&resource=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /logs`

List logs matching the provided filters. Logs are paginated by start and end timestamps.
There are more logs to fetch if `hasMore` is true in the response. Provide the `nextStartTime`
and `nextEndTime` timestamps as the `startTime` and `endTime` query parameters to fetch the next page of logs.

You can query for logs across multiple resources, but all resources must be in the same region and belong to the same owner.


<h3 id="list-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ownerId|query|string|true|The ID of the workspace to return logs for|
|startTime|query|string(date-time)|false|Epoch/Unix timestamp of start of time range to return. Defaults to `now() - 1 hour`.|
|endTime|query|string(date-time)|false|Epoch/Unix timestamp of end of time range to return. Defaults to `now()`.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to query logs for. Backward will return most recent logs first.<br>Forward will start with the oldest logs in the time range.<br>|
|resource|query|[string]|true|Filter logs by their resource. A resource is the id of a server, cronjob, job, postgres, redis, workflow, or sandbox group.|
|instance|query|[string]|false|Filter logs by the instance they were emitted from. An instance is the id of a specific running server.|
|host|query|[string]|false|Filter request logs by their host. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.|
|statusCode|query|[string]|false|Filter request logs by their status code. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.|
|method|query|[string]|false|Filter request logs by their requests method. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.|
|task|query|[string]|false|Filter logs by their task(s)|
|taskRun|query|[string]|false|Filter logs by their task run id(s)|
|sandbox|query|[string]|false|Filter logs by sandbox ID.|
|level|query|[string]|false|Filter logs by their severity level. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.|
|type|query|[string]|false|Filter logs by their type. Types include `app` for application logs, `request` for request logs, and `build` for build logs. You can find the full set of types available for a query by using the `GET /logs/values` endpoint.|
|text|query|[string]|false|Filter by the text of the logs. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.|
|path|query|[string]|false|Filter request logs by their path. [Wildcards and regex](https://render.com/docs/logging#wildcards-and-regular-expressions) are supported.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items to return. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|forward|
|direction|backward|

## Subscribe to new logs

<a id="opIdsubscribe-logs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.render.com/v1/logs/subscribe?ownerId=string&resource=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /logs/subscribe`

Open a websocket connection to subscribe to logs matching the provided filters. Logs are streamed in real-time as they are generated.

You can query for logs across multiple resources, but all resources must be in the same region and belong to the same owner.


<h3 id="subscribe-to-new-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ownerId|query|string|true|The ID of the workspace to return logs for|
|startTime|query|string(date-time)|false|Epoch/Unix timestamp of start of time range to return. Defaults to `now() - 1 hour`.|
|endTime|query|string(date-time)|false|Epoch/Unix timestamp of end of time range to return. Defaults to `now()`.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to query logs for. Backward will return most recent logs first.<br>Forward will start with the oldest logs in the time range.<br>|
|resource|query|[string]|true|Filter logs by their resource. A resource is the id of a server, cronjob, job, postgres, redis, workflow, or sandbox group.|
|instance|query|[string]|false|Filter logs by the instance they were emitted from. An instance is the id of a specific running server.|

<h1 id="render-public-api-maintenance">Maintenance</h1>

The `Maintenance` endpoints allow you to retrieve the latest maintenance runs for your Render services. You can also reschedule maintenance or trigger it to start immediately.

## Update maintenance run

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/maintenance/mrn-cph1rs3idesc73a2b2mg \
```

`PATCH /maintenance/{maintenanceRunID}`

|---|---|---|---|---|

## Trigger maintenance run

<a id="opIdtrigger-maintenance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/maintenance/mrn-cph1rs3idesc73a2b2mg/trigger \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /maintenance/{maintenanceRunID}/trigger`

Trigger the scheduled maintenance run with the provided ID.

Triggering maintenance is asynchronous. To check whether maintenance has started, use the [Retrieve maintenance run](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/retrieve-maintenance) endpoint.

As maintenance progresses, the run's `state` will change from `scheduled` to other values, such as `in_progress` and `succeeded`.


<h3 id="trigger-maintenance-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|maintenanceRunID|path|string|true|none|

## Get CPU usage

<a id="opIdget-cpu"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/metrics/cpu \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /metrics/cpu`

Get CPU usage for one or more resources.


<h3 id="get-cpu-usage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|endTime|query|string(date-time)|false|Epoch/Unix timestamp of end of time range to return. Defaults to `now()`.|
|resolutionSeconds|query|number|false|The resolution of the returned data|
|resource|query|string|false|Resource ID to query. When multiple resource query params are provided, they are ORed together. Resources can be service ids, Postgres ids, or Redis ids|
|service|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** This parameter is deprecated. Please use `resource` instead|
|instance|query|string|false|Instance ID to query. When multiple instance ID query params are provided, they are ORed together|
|aggregationMethod|query|string|false|The aggregation method to apply to multiple time series|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregationMethod|AVG|
|aggregationMethod|MAX|
|aggregationMethod|MIN|

```json
        "value": 1
      }

  }
]
```

## Get bandwidth usage breakdown by traffic source

<a id="opIdget-bandwidth-sources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/metrics/bandwidth-sources \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /metrics/bandwidth-sources`

Get bandwidth usage for one or more resources broken down by traffic source (HTTP, WebSocket, NAT, PrivateLink).

Returns hourly data points with traffic source breakdown. Traffic source data is available from March 9, 2025 onwards.
Queries for earlier dates will return a 400 Bad Request error.


<h3 id="get-bandwidth-usage-breakdown-by-traffic-source-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startTime|query|string(date-time)|false|Epoch/Unix timestamp of start of time range to return. Defaults to `now() - 1 hour`.|
|endTime|query|string(date-time)|false|Epoch/Unix timestamp of end of time range to return. Defaults to `now()`.|
|resource|query|string|false|Service ID to query. When multiple service ids are provided, they are ORed together|
|service|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** This parameter is deprecated. Please use `resource` instead|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "labels": {
        "resource": "srv-abc123",
        "trafficSource": "total"
      },
      "values": [
        {
          "timestamp": 1709856000,
          "value": 125.5
        },
        {
          "timestamp": 1709859600,
          "value": 98.2
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "labels": {
        "resource": "srv-abc123",
        "trafficSource": "http"
      },
      "values": [
        {
          "timestamp": 1709856000,
          "value": 100
        },
        {
          "timestamp": 1709859600,
          "value": 75.8
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "labels": {
        "resource": "srv-abc123",
        "trafficSource": "websocket"
      },
      "values": [
        {
          "timestamp": 1709856000,
          "value": 25.5
        },
        {
          "timestamp": 1709859600,
          "value": 22.4
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "bandwidth sources data is only available after 2025-03-09"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json

  "id": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "code": "string"
}
```

The error body's optional `code` field<br>identifies specific failures that clients can handle<br>machine-readably.<br><br>Error codes:<br>- `too_many_resources`: the query requests more resources than<br>  the breakdown supports (maximum 30)<br>|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h1 id="render-public-api-one-off-jobs">One-Off Jobs</h1>

[One-off jobs](https://render.com/docs/one-off-jobs) are standalone tasks that run to completion using the most recent successful build of an existing service.


## List jobs

<a id="opIdlist-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/services/string/jobs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /services/{serviceId}/jobs`

List jobs for the provided service that match the provided filters. If no filters are provided, all jobs for the service are returned.


<h3 id="list-jobs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cursor|query|string|false|The position in the result list to start from when fetching paginated results. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items to return. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|status|query|[string]|false|Filter for the status of the job (`pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `canceled`)|
|createdBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for jobs created before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|createdAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for jobs created after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|startedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for jobs started before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|startedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for jobs started after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|finishedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for jobs finished before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|finishedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for jobs finished after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|serviceId|path|string|true|The ID of the service|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|running|
|status|succeeded|
|status|failed|
|status|canceled|

> 200 Response

```json
  {
```

<h1 id="render-public-api-postgres">Postgres</h1>

[Postgres](https://render.com/docs/postgresql) endpoints enable you to interact with your Render Postgres databases.
You can manage databases, exports, recoveries, and failovers.


## List Postgres instances

<a id="opIdlist-postgres"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/postgres \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /postgres`

List Postgres instances matching the provided filters. If no filters are provided, all Postgres instances are returned.


<h3 id="list-postgres-instances-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Filter by name|
|region|query|[[region](#schemaregion)]|false|Filter by resource region|
|suspended|query|[string]|false|Filter resources based on whether they're suspended or not suspended|
|createdBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources created before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|createdAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources created after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|updatedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources updated before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|updatedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources updated after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|ownerId|query|[string]|false|The ID of the workspaces to return resources for|
|environmentId|query|[string]|false|Filter for resources that belong to an environment|
|includeReplicas|query|boolean|false|Include replicas in the response|
|cursor|query|string|false|The position in the result list to start from when fetching paginated results. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items to return. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|

```bash
    "connectionPool": "none",

        "description": "string"
      }

    "version": "11"
  }'
```

## Trigger point-in-time recovery

<a id="opIdrecover-postgres"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/postgres/string/recovery \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "restoreName": "string",
    "restoreTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "datadogApiKey": "string",
    "datadogSite": "string",
    "plan": "string",
    "environmentId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /postgres/{postgresId}/recovery`

Trigger [point-in-time recovery](https://render.com/docs/postgresql-backups) on the Postgres instance with the provided ID.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "restoreName": "string",
  "restoreTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "datadogApiKey": "string",
  "datadogSite": "string",
  "plan": "string",
  "environmentId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="trigger-point-in-time-recovery-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|postgresId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» restoreName|body|string|false|Name of the new database.|
|» restoreTime|body|string(date-time)|false|The point in time to restore the database to. See `/recovery-info` for restore availability|
|» datadogApiKey|body|string|false|Datadog API key to use for monitoring the new database. Defaults to the API key of the original database. Use an empty string to prevent copying of the API key to the new database.|
|» datadogSite|body|string|false|Datadog region code to use for monitoring the new database. Defaults to the region code of the original database. Use an empty string to prevent copying of the region code to the new database.|
|» plan|body|string|false|The plan to use for the new database. Defaults to the same plan as the original database. Cannot be a lower tier plan than the original database.|
|» environmentId|body|string|false|The environment to create the new database in. Defaults to the environment of the original database.|

## Delete project

<a id="opIddelete-project"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/projects/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /projects/{projectId}`

Delete the project with the provided ID.

Requires _all_ of the project's environments to be empty (i.e., they must contain no services or other resources). Otherwise, deletion fails with a `409` response.

To delete a non-empty project, do one of the following:

<h1 id="render-public-api-services">Services</h1>

[Services](https://render.com/docs/service-types) allow you to manage your web services, private services, background workers, cron jobs, and static sites.


## List services

<a id="opIdlist-services"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/services \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /services`

List services matching the provided filters. If no filters are provided, returns all services you have permissions to view.


<h3 id="list-services-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|[string]|false|Filter by name|
|type|query|[[serviceType](#schemaservicetype)]|false|Filter for types of services|
|environmentId|query|[string]|false|Filter for resources that belong to an environment|
|env|query|[[serviceRuntime](#schemaserviceruntime)]|false|**Deprecated.** Filter for environments (runtimes) of services (deprecated; use `runtime` instead)|
|region|query|[[region](#schemaregion)]|false|Filter by resource region|
|suspended|query|[string]|false|Filter resources based on whether they're suspended or not suspended|
|createdBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources created before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|createdAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources created after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|updatedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources updated before a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|updatedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter for resources updated after a certain time (specified as an ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|ownerId|query|[string]|false|The ID of the workspaces to return resources for|
|includePreviews|query|boolean|false|Include previews in the response|
|cursor|query|string|false|The position in the result list to start from when fetching paginated results. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items to return. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|

## Create service

<a id="opIdcreate-service"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/services \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "static_site",
    "name": "string",
    "ownerId": "string",
    "repo": "https://github.com/render-examples/flask-hello-world",
    "autoDeploy": "yes",
    "autoDeployTrigger": "commit",
    "branch": "string",
    "image": {
      "ownerId": "string",
      "registryCredentialId": "string",
      "imagePath": "string"
    },
    "buildFilter": {
      "paths": [
        "string"
      ],
      "ignoredPaths": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "rootDir": "string",
    "envVars": [
      {
        "key": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "secretFiles": [
      {
        "name": "string",
        "content": "string"
      }
    ],
    "environmentId": "string",
    "serviceDetails": {
      "buildCommand": "string",
      "headers": [
        {
          "path": "/static/*",
          "name": "Cache-Control",
          "value": "public, max-age=604800"
        }
      ],
      "publishPath": "string",
      "pullRequestPreviewsEnabled": "no",
      "previews": {
        "generation": "off"
      },
      "routes": [
        {
          "type": "redirect",
          "source": "/:bar/foo",
          "destination": "/foo/:bar",
          "priority": 0
        }
      ],
      "renderSubdomainPolicy": "enabled",
      "ipAllowList": [
        {
          "cidrBlock": "string",
          "description": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /services`

Creates a new Render service in the specified workspace with the specified configuration.

400 with `code: build_source_region_mismatch` if `buildSourceId` names a git-backed
Build Source in a different region than the service.

<h3 id="create-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[servicePOST](#schemaservicepost)|true|none|
|» type|body|[serviceType](#schemaservicetype)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The service's name. Must be unique within the workspace.|
|» ownerId|body|string|true|The ID of the workspace the service belongs to. Obtain your workspace's ID from its Settings page in the Render Dashboard.|

|» autoDeploy|body|[autoDeploy](#schemaautodeploy)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: use `autoDeployTrigger` instead. You can't set both `autoDeploy` and `autoDeployTrigger` in the same request.<br><br>- `yes` is equivalent to `autoDeployTrigger: commit`.<br>- `no` is equivalent to `autoDeployTrigger: off`.<br>|
|» autoDeployTrigger|body|string|false|Controls autodeploy behavior.<br><br>- `commit`: Deploy each time a commit is pushed to the service's linked branch.<br>- `checksPass`: Deploy each time a commit is pushed to the linked branch, but only after the commit's CI checks pass.<br>- `off`: Disable autodeploys.<br>|
|» branch|body|string|false|The repo branch to pull, build, and deploy. If omitted, uses the repository's default branch.|

|» buildSourceId|body|string|false|The ID of the Build Source to link this service to. Cannot be combined with build-configuration changes or other `serviceDetails` fields, except `startCommand`. Linking to a Build Source with a native runtime requires a start command, either in this request or already set on the service. |» » *oneOf*|body|[staticSiteDetailsPATCH](#schemastaticsitedetailspatch)|false|none|

## Create service preview (image-backed)

<a id="opIdpreview-service"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/services/string/preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "imagePath": "docker.io/library/nginx:latest",
    "name": "preview",
    "plan": "starter"
  }'
```

`POST /services/{serviceId}/preview`

Create a preview instance for an image-backed service. The preview uses the settings of the base service (referenced by `serviceId`), except settings overridden via provided parameters.

View all active previews from your service's Previews tab in the Render Dashboard.

Note that you can't create previews for Git-backed services using the Render API.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "imagePath": "docker.io/library/nginx:latest",
  "name": "preview",
  "plan": "starter"
}
```

<h3 id="create-service-preview-image-backed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serviceId|path|string|true|The ID of the service|
|body|body|[previewInput](#schemapreviewinput)|true|none|
|» imagePath|body|string|true|Must be either a full URL or the relative path to an image. If a relative path, Render uses the base service's image URL as its root. For example, if the base service's image URL is `docker.io/library/nginx:latest`, then valid values are: `docker.io/library/nginx:<any tag or SHA>`, `library/nginx:<any tag or SHA>`, or `nginx:<any tag or SHA>`. Note that the path must match (only the tag or SHA can vary).|
|» name|body|string|false|A name for the service preview instance. If not specified, Render generates the name using the base service's name and the specified tag or SHA.|
|» plan|body|[plan](#schemaplan)|false|The compute plan to use. Legacy variants (`*_legacy`) identify grandfathered plans no longer offered for new services. Note that base services on any paid compute plan can't create preview instances with the `free` plan.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» plan|starter|
|» plan|starter_plus|
|» plan|standard|
|» plan|standard_plus|
|» plan|pro|
|» plan|pro_plus|
|» plan|pro_max|
|» plan|pro_ultra|
|» plan|free|
|» plan|custom|
|» plan|starter_legacy|
|» plan|standard_legacy|
|» plan|standard_plus_legacy|
|» plan|pro_legacy|
|» plan|pro_plus_legacy|
|» plan|0.5c-512mb|
|» plan|1c-2g|
|» plan|2c-4g|
|» plan|2c-8g|
|» plan|2c-16g|
|» plan|4c-8g|
|» plan|4c-16g|
|» plan|4c-32g|
|» plan|8c-16g|
|» plan|8c-32g|
|» plan|8c-64g|
|» plan|12c-24g|
|» plan|12c-48g|
|» plan|12c-96g|

<h1 id="render-public-api-services---headers">Services - Headers</h1>

Use HTTP headers to inject response headers in static site responses. You can also use wildcards like /path/* to add headers to responses for all matching request paths.

## List header rules

<h3 id="list-header-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|path|query|[string]|false|Filter for specific paths that headers apply to|

|value|query|[string]|false|Filter for header values|
|cursor|query|string|false|The position in the result list to start from when fetching paginated results. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items to return. For details, see [Pagination](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/pagination).|

<h1 id="render-public-api-services---routes">Services - Routes</h1>

Add Redirect or Rewrite Rules to modify requests to your site without writing code. You can use URL parameters to capture path segments, and wildcards to redirect everything under a given path.

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/services/string/routes \
```

## Update redirect/rewrite rule priority

<a id="opIdpatch-route"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/services/string/routes/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "priority": 0
  }'
```

`PATCH /services/{serviceId}/routes/{routeId}`

Update the priority for a particular redirect/rewrite rule.

To apply redirect/rewrite rules to an incoming request, Render starts from the rule with priority `0` and applies the first encountered rule that matches the request's path (if any).

Render increments the priority of other rules by `1` as necessary to make space for the updated rule.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "priority": 0
}
```

<h3 id="update-redirectrewrite-rule-priority-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serviceId|path|string|true|The ID of the service|
|routeId|path|string|true|The id of the route|
|body|body|[routePatch](#schemaroutepatch)|true|none|
|» priority|body|integer|true|Redirect and Rewrite Rules are applied in priority order starting at 0. Moves this route to the specified priority and adjusts other route priorities accordingly.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "headers": {
    "id": "string",
    "type": "redirect",
    "source": "string",
    "destination": "string",
    "priority": 0
  }
}
```

```json
}
```

## Create a build source

<a id="opIdcreate-build-source"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/build-sources \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ownerId": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "projectId": "string",
    "git": {
      "branch": "string",
      "buildCommand": "string",
      "buildFilter": {
        "paths": [
          "string"
        ],
        "ignoredPaths": [
          "string"
        ]
      },
      "dockerContext": "string",
      "dockerfilePath": "string",
      "runtime": "docker",
      "registryCredentialId": "string",
      "region": "oregon",
      "repoUrl": "string",
      "rootDir": "string"
    },
    "image": {
      "ownerId": "string",
      "registryCredentialId": "string",
      "imageUrl": "string"
    },
    "serviceIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "envVars": [
      {
        "key": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "secretFiles": [
      {
        "name": "string",
        "content": "string"
      }
    ],
    "envGroupIds": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /build-sources`

Create a build source that can be linked to one or more
services in the same workspace.

Exactly one of `git` or `image` must be set:
- `git`: the build source is git-backed. The code is built in
   the requested `region` (defaults to `oregon`).
- `image`: the build source is image-backed. It points at an
  existing image in an external registry; no build is performed.

`envVars`, `secretFiles`, and `envGroupIds` set the build-time
environment and are only valid for `git` sources; the request fails
if any are provided with `image`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ownerId": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "projectId": "string",
  "git": {
    "branch": "string",
    "buildCommand": "string",
    "buildFilter": {
      "paths": [
        "string"
      ],
      "ignoredPaths": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "dockerContext": "string",
    "dockerfilePath": "string",
    "runtime": "docker",
    "registryCredentialId": "string",
    "region": "oregon",
    "repoUrl": "string",
    "rootDir": "string"
  },
  "image": {
    "ownerId": "string",
    "registryCredentialId": "string",
    "imageUrl": "string"
  },
  "serviceIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "envVars": [
    {
      "key": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "secretFiles": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "content": "string"
    }
  ],
  "envGroupIds": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|» ownerId|body|string|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|

|» » branch|body|string|false|none|

|» » buildFilter|body|object|false|Glob patterns matched against files changed by a commit. When set, a commit only triggers a build when at least one changed file matches `paths` and none match `ignoredPaths`. Useful for monorepos where a single repo backs many services.<br>|
|» » » paths|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » » ignoredPaths|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » dockerContext|body|string|false|Directory passed to `docker build` as the build context, relative to the repository root. Only valid for the `docker` runtime. Defaults to ".".<br>|
|» » dockerfilePath|body|string|false|none|
|» » runtime|body|string|true|Build runtime for the build source. Static sites are not supported for build sources.<br>|
|» » registryCredentialId|body|string|false|none|

## Update a build source

<a id="opIdupdate-build-source"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/build-sources/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "git": {
      "branch": "string",
      "buildCommand": "string",
      "buildFilter": {
        "paths": [
          "string"
        ],
        "ignoredPaths": [
          "string"
        ]
      },
      "dockerContext": "string",
      "dockerfilePath": "string",
      "runtime": "docker",
      "registryCredentialId": "string",
      "region": "frankfurt",
      "repoUrl": "string",
      "rootDir": "string"
    },
    "image": {
      "imageUrl": "string",
      "registryCredentialId": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /build-sources/{buildSourceId}`

Update a shared build source. Each top-level field is a true patch,
unset fields are left unchanged.

Supplying `git` or `image` can change the build source's
underlying identity:
- `image` on a git-backed build source switches it to image-backed
- `git` on an image-backed build source switches it to git-backed
- `git` on a build source that's already git-backed is a pure
  patch onto the existing config


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "git": {
    "branch": "string",
    "buildCommand": "string",
    "buildFilter": {
      "paths": [
        "string"
      ],
      "ignoredPaths": [
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "dockerContext": "string",
    "dockerfilePath": "string",
    "runtime": "docker",
    "registryCredentialId": "string",
    "region": "frankfurt",
    "repoUrl": "string",
    "rootDir": "string"
  },
  "image": {
    "imageUrl": "string",
    "registryCredentialId": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-build-source-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildSourceId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» git|body|object|false|none|
|» » branch|body|string|false|none|
|» » buildCommand|body|string|false|none|
|» » buildFilter|body|object|false|Glob patterns matched against files changed by a commit. When set, a commit only triggers a build when at least one changed file matches `paths` and none match `ignoredPaths`. Useful for monorepos where a single repo backs many services.<br>|
|» » » paths|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » » ignoredPaths|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » dockerContext|body|string|false|Directory passed to `docker build` as the build context, relative to the repository root. Only valid for the `docker` runtime.<br>|
|» » dockerfilePath|body|string|false|none|
|» » runtime|body|string|false|Build runtime for the build source. Static sites are not supported for build sources.<br>|
|» » registryCredentialId|body|string|false|Optional reference to the registry credential for this build. Omit the field to leave the stored credential unchanged; send an empty string to clear it.<br>|
|» » region|body|string|false|Region for the build. Honored only when this PATCH performs an image→build transition; rejected on a pure build patch (the cluster is pinned for an existing build), and must match the prior build region when switching back to build after time as an external image. Defaults to "oregon" for first-time builds.<br>|
|» » repoUrl|body|string|false|none|
|» » rootDir|body|string|false|none|
|» image|body|object|false|Patch shape for a build source's image identity. Unset fields are left unchanged on the underlying image reference. ownerId is intentionally omitted — a build source's owner is fixed at creation, and changing the image's owner would amount to a different identity.<br>|
|» » imageUrl|body|string|false|none|
|» » registryCredentialId|body|string|false|Optional reference to the registry credential passed to the image repository to retrieve this image. Omit the field to leave the stored credential unchanged; send an empty string to clear it.<br>|

## Trigger a build

<a id="opIdtrigger-build-source-build"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/build-sources/string/builds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /build-sources/{buildSourceId}/builds`

Start a new build of the build source at the current HEAD of its
branch, even if an up-to-date build already exists. Services linked to
the build source with autodeploy enabled are deployed with the result.

Updating a build source or its build-time environment (env vars,
secret files, env groups) with the REST API does not build it. Call
this endpoint after those changes to build them.

Only `git` build sources can be built.


<h3 id="trigger-a-build-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildSourceId|path|string|true|none|

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/workflows \
  -X POST \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

    "name": "string",
    "ownerId": "string",

      "branch": "string",
      "buildCommand": "string",
      "repo": "string",
      "rootDir": "string",

    },

        "value": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## Run task

<a id="opIdcreateTask"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.render.com/v1/task-runs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "task": "my-workflow-slug/my-task, my-workflow-slug/my-task:SHA123",
    "input": [
      null
    ],
    "idempotencyKey": "6b2f1f7a-6a0e-4f6f-9d1a-2b1d0d5f6c11"
  }'
```

`POST /task-runs`

Kicks off a run of the workflow task with the provided ID, passing the provided input data.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "task": "my-workflow-slug/my-task, my-workflow-slug/my-task:SHA123",
  "input": [
    null
  ],
  "idempotencyKey": "6b2f1f7a-6a0e-4f6f-9d1a-2b1d0d5f6c11"
}
```

<h3 id="run-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» task|body|string|true|A task slug in the format workflow-slug/task-name. An optional version can be appended (workflow-slug/task-name:version). If no version is provided, the latest version is used. Cannot be blank.|
|» input|body|[object] \| object|true|Input data for a task. Can be either an array (for positional arguments) or an object (for named parameters).|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[object]|false|Positional arguments passed to the task function|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|Named parameters passed to the task function as keyword arguments|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» idempotencyKey|body|string|false|A client-generated key that makes starting a task run safe to retry. Repeating a request with the same key within 24 hours returns the task run that the first request started instead of starting another one; the repeated request's input is ignored. Keys are scoped to a workflow. Omit the key to always start a new run.|

## Stream realtime events (SSE)

<a id="opIdstreamTaskRunsEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.render.com/v1/task-runs/events?taskRunIds=trn-1234&taskRunIds=trn-5678' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /task-runs/events`

Establishes a unidirectional event stream. The server sends events as lines
formatted per the SSE spec. Clients should set `Accept: text/event-stream`
and keep the connection open.

The server sends a `task.completed` event whenever a requested task run reaches
any terminal state (`completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`).
The `status` field of the payload indicates which state was reached.

The server automatically closes the stream in the following cases:

- All requested task runs have reached a terminal state.
- The stream has not sent any events for 30 minutes.

For tasks with a timeout higher than 30 minutes, waiting clients should fall back
to polling with the [Retrieve task run](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/gettaskrun)
endpoint.


<h3 id="stream-realtime-events-sse-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|taskRunIds|query|[string]|true|Filter to a subset of task run IDs.|
|Accept|header|string|false|Must be `text/event-stream`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Accept|text/event-stream|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```text
event: task.completed
data: {
        "id": "string",
        "taskId": "string",
        "status": "pending",
        "results": [
          "string"
        ],
        "error": "string",
        "startedAt": "2025-09-04T17:25:17.979Z",
        "completedAt": "2025-09-04T17:25:17.979Z"
      }

```

The machine-readable codes that can appear in the error object's "code" field. The field is a plain string so new codes are not breaking changes; this vocabulary exists so generated clients get typed constants. OpenAPI cannot deprecate individual enum values, so deprecation notes live in x-enum-descriptions.

<h2 id="tocS_DeployMode">DeployMode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadeploymode"></a>
<a id="schema_DeployMode"></a>
<a id="tocSdeploymode"></a>
<a id="tocsdeploymode"></a>

```json
"build_and_deploy"
```

Controls deployment behavior when triggering a deploy.

- `deploy_only`: Deploy the last successful build without rebuilding (minimizes downtime)
- `build_and_deploy`: Build new code and deploy it (default behavior when not specified)

**Note:** `deployMode` cannot be combined with `buildId`. `deploy_only` cannot be combined with
`commitId`, `imageUrl`, or `clearCache`, as those are build related fields.
